result.text:
Yes. AT&T discontinued its email-to-text service on June 17, 2025. This is confirmed by AT&T's official support website.

According to AT&T, the shutdown affects both directions of messaging.

What no longer works?

Email to text: Sending an email to a phone number followed by (at)txt.att.net or (at)mms.att.net no longer delivers a text message.

Text to email: AT&T customers can no longer use the carrier's gateway to send text messages to email addresses.

Regular texting: Ordinary SMS and MMS messages between phones continue to work normally.

Regular email: Email services such as Gmail and Outlook are unaffected.

What can you use instead?

It depends on how you used the service:

For personal use: Send a regular text from your phone, or use a messaging app.

For automated alerts or notifications: Use an email-to-SMS service or messaging provider that supports delivery to AT&T numbers. Twilio offers options for replacing the old carrier gateway.

AT&T has not announced a replacement for its old public email-to-text gateway.

Can I ask what you used AT&T email-to-text for? For example, sending emails to your own phone, receiving automated computer or security alerts, or sending texts to other AT&T customers. I can suggest the most practical alternative for your situation.
